claim: The docs.influxdata.com Telegraf MQTT Producer page documents the same keep-alive hazard as the GitHub README: mosquitto v2.0.12+ requires non-zero keep_alive or returns 'identifier rejected', with paho.golang's reference default of 30
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must configure an explicit non-zero MQTT keep-alive
scope_conditions: Telegraf v1 docs MQTT Producer output; mosquitto >= v2.0.12
quoted_support: In v2.0.12+ of the mosquitto MQTT server, there is a bug requiring the keep_alive value to be set non-zero in Telegraf. Otherwise, the server will return with identifier rejected. As a reference eclipse/paho.golang sets the keep_alive to 30.

claim: The official Telegraf docs page confirms the Homie-v4 layout's lifecycle limitation: no dynamic MQTT 'will' is possible due to client-library limits, so devices are only marked lost on clean exit and may stay wrongly ready after abnormal aborts
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's LWT-based availability design is a genuine differentiator over the incumbent Telegraf pattern
scope_conditions: Telegraf MQTT Producer output homie-v4 layout
quoted_support: Due to limitations in the MQTT client library, it is not possible to set a "will" dynamically. In consequence, devices are only marked lost when exiting Telegraf normally and might not change in abnormal aborts.

claim: Telegraf's MQTT output supports MQTT 5 publish properties (content_type, response_topic, message_expiry, topic_alias, and user_properties) only when protocol is set to 5, and these must be defined at the end of the plugin config due to TOML parsing
stance_target: MQTT5 feature surface an agent publisher can adopt (message expiry in particular is useful for stale-telemetry detection)
quoted_support: ## Optional MQTT 5 publish properties ## These setting only apply if the "protocol" property is set to 5. This must be defined at the end of the plugin settings, otherwise TOML will assume anything else is part of this table.

claim: The Telegraf 'field' layout example demonstrates the value-per-leaf-topic sensor pattern the HA ecosystem already consumes: 'telegraf/modbus/device 1/temperature 21.4' — one retained-style topic per metric field with the bare value as string
stance_target: HA-friendly MQTT sensor topic conventions; per-field topics are proven prior art for ha-linux-agent's topic design
scope_conditions: Telegraf MQTT Producer output, field layout
quoted_support: telegraf/modbus/device 1/temperature    21.4 ... NOTE: Only fields will be output, tags and the timestamp are omitted.

claim: Telegraf's homie-v4 device tree publishes Homie lifecycle attributes ($homie '4.0', $name, $state 'ready', $nodes, per-node $name/$properties/$datatype) — a fully declarative self-describing device model an agent could adopt without the churn limitation
stance_target: self-describing MQTT device models are established prior art for fleet agents; the pattern is sound, Telegraf's dynamic-metric implementation is what breaks it
scope_conditions: Telegraf MQTT Producer output, homie-v4 layout

claim: Telegraf supports secret-store-backed MQTT credentials: the username and password options can be sourced from secret stores rather than hardcoded
stance_target: fleet-wide credential management pattern for jupiterOS — broker credentials should come from a secret store, not plaintext config
quoted_support: This plugin supports secrets from secret stores for the username and password option.
